P1.evidence: No setter notes or application were referenced at any point on this call, unlike the two calls the day before where Derek's notes and the written application were both read back. The frame covered two of four parts: 'go through where you're at at the moment, just over everything and then also where you want to go. See if we can help you with that. If not, I'll point you in the best direction.' Agreement obtained ('Sounds good? Perfect.'). Open question asked verbatim: 'So tell me, what can we potentially help you out with, Nicholas?'

P2.evidence: The injury probe was the best part: 'what sort of mobility things do you have coming up now? Do you already, like, have constant pains, flare-ups?' surfaced the shoulder, the lumbar injury with its five-month timeline and six weeks of chiropractic care, and later the knee. Age was asked (33). Body fat was probed. Nutrition was asked and probed to frequency. But height and weight were never asked, health conditions were never asked, training days per week were never established, results were never asked, and sleep and energy were never asked.

P3.evidence: Strong surface work with a good one-to-ten and a vivid picture of the target self. P3c ran well: 'do you feel like you can still really ski or is it like you're being limited as well with your knee, with your lower back?' The reflect-back was clean: 'the physical is just a by-product of feeling better, getting rid of the pain. Being able to just play games with your friends.' But the depth stopped at friends and volleyball — the rep never asked who else this impacts and never drove to identity or longevity on a 33-year-old with three unresolved injuries who is visibly afraid of decline.

P4.evidence: 'why can't you not train them at the moment?' and 'Why do you feel like you're not able to train them correctly at the moment?' were genuine root-cause probes, and the prospect named the gap himself: 'I need to find something different and then a little more just accountability also.' But the rep then closed the phase with reassurance rather than excavation — 'do you feel like your commitment would stop you from actually following through with it? No. Not that I'm not. I don't think so. Okay, check' — which is the opposite of the scripted move.

P5.evidence: P5b ran twice and well: 'would you be willing to let it stay the same as it is at the moment, or even let it get worse when it comes to your mobility and flexibility?' then 'Are you okay with that outcome?' But the prospect answered that he would be fine with decline if he had not tried — 'if I'm sitting there doing nothing and things get worse, I'm not going to get mad. I'm just going to understand' — and instead of asking why not, the rep reframed and moved to agreement. No two-year picture, no line in the sand.

P6.evidence: Best commitment check in the batch. P6b ran clean before any price was mentioned: 'let's say we start working together... would there be anything else that would stop you from actually putting in the work and getting the outcome out of it where you're going to feel better, where the pain is going to go away?' followed up with 'do you feel like your commitment would stop you?' A genuine yes was in hand before presenting: 'at this point, I'm kind of looking forward to getting started.'

P11.evidence: Payment collected live through a card decline and a second card. Trevor onboarding booked for Tuesday and confirmed in the prospect's inbox. Skool access verified live by having him click each tab. Onboarding form confirmed received with instructions to complete before Tuesday. Only P11c falls short: the agreement email arrived but was not signed on the call, and when the prospect asked directly what was in it the rep did not walk through it.

objection_plays.detail: The trigger was liquidity rather than affordability. Savings were asked ($3,000), income and pay cycle were asked ($5,000 every two weeks, next in one week), investments were volunteered (stocks). A plan was structured live and then restructured on request. Never ran: the isolation move ('finances aside, nothing else keeping you from 100%'), how many credit cards, available credit per card, used versus available. The play was not needed at length here, but the scripted isolation was skipped entirely.

A contract-scrutiny objection with no scripted play: 'Is this a free coaching extension? I'm not missing anything in that contract, am I?' There is no path in the script for a prospect asking what is in the agreement at the point of signature. The rep answered 'it's very straightforward' without opening it and offered a verbal continuation promise instead. This is a script gap worth closing, not a rep failure alone.

notes: Textbook Phase 6 and Phase 11 — the commitment was genuine before the price was named, and every onboarding step except signature was completed on the call. The process gap is Phase 5: the prospect said he would accept decline without regret if he had not tried, and that was left standing. The far more important gap is not in the script at all — three unresolved injuries, one of them five months old and still symptomatic, were used as selling material rather than triggering a clearance question.
